sentences.show: On this day in 1928, Alexander Fleming confirmed the accident behind the first antibiotic.
That summer, he left dishes of bacteria out and went on holiday.
When he came back, one dish had gone mouldy.
Around the mould, the bacteria were gone.
On the 28th, a new experiment confirmed it.
The mould was releasing something that killed bacteria.
He called it “mould juice” — and later, penicillin.
In Oxford, Howard Florey and Ernst Chain turned it into a medicine.
By D-Day, there was enough for every wounded Allied soldier.
In 1945, the three shared the Nobel Prize.
His words: “One sometimes finds what one is not looking for.”
Every day has a story like this.
